key_insight: FrontierMat exposes a gap between plausible answers and experimentally grounded reasoning in frontier materials R&D.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark tests whether language models can infer research outcomes from experimental evidence, including mechanisms spanning multiple scales.
method: Build 330 expert-validated problems from frontier academic and industrial studies.
Annotate functional domain, material system and mechanism scale; include 130 cross-scale problems.
Adapt an open-weight model using meta-weighted continued pretraining and scale-modular self-distillation.
evidence_signal: The strongest general-purpose model scores 53.7%; cross-scale problems score 8.7 percentage points below matched single-scale problems, while domain adaptation raises an open-weight model from 36.7% to 55.4%.
watch_item: Benchmark gains do not establish reliability in live R&D; experimentally plausible but incorrect conclusions remain a key risk.
paper_title: FrontierMat: Benchmarking Language Models at the Frontier of Materials R&D
